sentences: I measure 15 grams of whole coffee beans on a digital scale each morning before I start brewing.
I grind the beans to a medium-fine consistency using a burr grinder set to the number twelve.
I rinse the paper filter with hot water to remove any paper dust before adding the grounds.
I heat water in a kettle until it reaches 200 degrees Fahrenheit, then let it sit for thirty seconds.
I pour a small amount of water over the grounds to start the bloom and wait for it to bubble.
I pour the remaining water in a slow circular motion, keeping the water level steady in the dripper.
I set a timer for three minutes and check the progress of the drip every thirty seconds.
I stir the coffee grounds gently with a spoon after the initial pour to ensure even extraction.
I press the plunger of the French press down slowly and steadily after waiting four minutes.
I disassemble the French press and wash each part with warm soapy water after brewing.
I fill the coffee maker's reservoir with filtered water up to the twelve-cup mark.
I run a descaling solution through the coffee maker once every three months to remove mineral buildup.
I replace the water filter in the coffee maker every two months according to the manufacturer's instructions.
I wipe the counter with a damp cloth to clean up any spilled coffee grounds or water.
I dump the used coffee grounds into the compost bin and rinse the filter basket.
I rinse the carafe with hot water and let it dry upside down on a dish rack.
I set up the drip coffee maker by placing a paper filter in the basket and adding ground coffee.
I measure the water with a measuring cup and pour it into the reservoir of the drip machine.
I tamp the espresso grounds with a tamper to create a level and compact puck.
I pull a shot of espresso and watch the liquid stream into the small cup.
